sources.title: Reproducible processed-event, outbox and retry state-model test

claims.text: Kafka 4.3 documents that enable.idempotence prevents producer-retry duplicates, and that transactional.id implies idempotence and provides recovery semantics across producer sessions; the candidate limits this to Kafka transport semantics.
Kafka consumer documentation states that read_committed returns only committed transactional messages and may stop at the Last Stable Offset while transactions remain in flight.

Kafka delivery semantics documentation states that exactly-once requires cooperation with the destination storage system and explains coordinating consumer position with stored output. The candidate uses a single database transaction for processed-event state, business state, and outbox as its proposed destination-side design.

The capacity values, processed-event schema, outbox flow, retry/degradation/compensation, observability, and rollout procedure are explicit design assumptions and acceptance requirements, not claims about a particular deployed system.

The executable state-model test verifies that duplicate delivery after an uncommitted offset does not create a second business or outbox record, and that a relay retry retains the same downstream event ID after an ambiguous send. The candidate explicitly requires production database transaction/unique-constraint and downstream-idempotency contracts in addition to this model.

findings: 场景假设缺少端到端 SLO/业务规模或待澄清验收目标。
